incident.symptom: A chat-local Composio LinkedIn connection returned REVOKED_ACCESS_TOKEN / insufficient organization scope and was reported as a company-page publishing blocker.
incident.root_cause: Chat-local connector state was treated as if it were the canonical Powerhouse production OAuth authority. The production runtime uses a separate capability-proven connected account and had already published the company post.
incident.consequence: The user was unnecessarily asked to reconnect LinkedIn and extra aliases risked being created even though production already had a valid organization-scoped connection.

prevention: PRODUCTION_RUNTIME_BEFORE_CHAT_CONNECTOR: read canonical Brain runtime state before reporting OAuth blockers.
PROVIDER_URN_BEFORE_RECONNECT: inspect the current obligation for a durable provider ID before any reconnect or retry.
CHAT_SESSION_IS_DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY: a chat-local Composio connection cannot downgrade healthy production capability.
HUMAN_OAUTH_ONLY_ON_PRODUCTION_HARD_BOUNDARY: request user authorization only when canonical production capability is unavailable and no provider side effect exists.
NO_ALIAS_PROLIFERATION: do not create extra LinkedIn aliases as a generic recovery mechanism.
evidence: Canonical Brain state linkedin-composio-setup-current-state-v1 was ACTIVE with company_ready=true at the time the chat-local connector reported revoked or insufficient-scope credentials.
The canonical company organization is urn:li:organization:18234216 and the production account carried r_organization_admin and w_organization_social.
The 2026-09-29 linkedin_company publication obligation already contained provider_create_success=true and provider URN urn:li:share:7510609161110482944.
The same obligation records republish_forbidden=true and terminal_provider_side_effect=true, proving that reconnect-driven republication would be unsafe.
Provider-level evidence therefore demonstrates chat-session credential divergence rather than a production LinkedIn outage.
